newsitem.title: UK: OPEC says Iraq oil likely to depress crude prices.
newsitem.headline: OPEC says Iraq oil likely to depress crude prices.

text.p: Resumed Iraqi oil exports should see a contraseasonal 500-600,000 barrels per day (bpd) build in world oil stocks during the first quarter of next year and downward pressure on oil prices, OPEC's Vienna-based secretariat said on Monday.
The expected stockbuild would contrast sharply with a 1.2 million bpd stockdraw last year caused by a severe cold spell and production disruptions, the secretariat said in a monthly report.
"The implication of this would be downward pressure on prices during the first quarter of 1997 and possibly for the remainder of the year," it said.
The report contrasts with recent statements from OPEC member country oil ministers.

Several ministers in recent weeks have said they believe world oil markets would be strong enough to absorb the limited amount of Iraqi oil allowed on the markets for the first time in six years under the UN's oil-for-food exchange.
Without Iraq's return, assuming stable OPEC output at 26 million bpd, the first quarter 1997 market would have been balanced, the OPEC report added.
Stocks in the fourth quarter of 1996 were being built at 300,000 bpd, also normally a period of stockdraw, the secretariat said.
The report also showed a downward revision in the secretariat's estimate for the call on OPEC crude next year of 100,000 barrels a day (bpd) from last month's report to 25.1 million.
That compares with a 25.2 million for this year, up 100,000 bpd from last month's report.
The secretariat forecast world demand next year would climb 1.6 million bpd to 70.8 million with non-OPEC supply rising 1.7 million bpd to 45.7 million.
It projected the call for OPEC crude next year at 26 million bpd in the first quarter of 1997, followed by 23.7 million, 24.4 million and 26.4 million for following quarters of the year.
